title: Cost-Quality Sentry: Thresholds & Instrumentation for Low-cost Config Rollouts (Draft)
content:
Executive summary:

This is a working draft proposing a lightweight "cost-quality sentry" that enforces evaluation and telemetry thresholds when rolling cheaper inference configurations (quantized weights, smaller model variants, aggressive batching/caching) into production. The goal: enable meaningful unit-cost reductions while bounding user-facing quality regressions and making rollouts automatable and observable.

Why this now:
- We have several workload patterns where cheaper configs (4-bit, 8-bit, smaller families) reduce token cost by 30–70% but occasionally introduce subtle quality regressions that only appear for corner-case prompts.
- Current rollouts depend heavily on manual spot-checks and ad-hoc heuristics; we need a reproducible gating surface that product, SRE, and CS teams can rely on.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: hosted API and Dedicated deployments where model variant substitution is possible. Focus on text generation/chat workloads and reranking pipelines used by customers.
- Non-goal: defining absolute ML model acceptance thresholds for model onboarding (that remains applied by applied-ML). This is about operational rollouts of cheaper configurations for already onboarded models.

Definitions (for this doc):
- Cheaper config: any change intended to reduce per-token or per-request unit cost (quantization level change, smaller model family, reduced seq-length cap, aggressive cache TTLs, increased batching target).
- Quality delta (Qd): a normalized metric in [ -1.0 , +1.0 ] representing degradation (+ = improvement, - = regression) aggregated from a workload-specific eval suite (task-weighted).
- Cost delta (Cd): percent reduction in per-token or per-request cost (e.g., -45% means 45% cheaper).
- Cost-of-quality ratio (CQR): Cd / |Qd| when Qd < 0; heuristic for how much cost we gain per unit quality lost. Higher is better.

Proposed guardrail principles:
1) Two-tier gates: rapid canary + extended silent canary
   - Rapid canary: small subset of traffic (0.5%–2%) for immediate automated checks (latency, error rate, token-level basic quality triggers) with 30–60 minute evaluation window.
   - Extended silent canary: larger subset (5%–15%) with additional offline eval metrics and human-notified dashboards for 24–72 hours before wider rollout.
2) Multi-metric quality profile: don't rely on a single metric. Composite should include: automated eval-suite Qd, user-facing signal proxies (e.g., fallback rate, retry rate, truncated-response fraction), and customer-facing telemetry if available (CS escalations).
3) Tiered thresholds: more conservative thresholds for lower-risk workloads (high-frequency user-facing flows) and looser for low-impact async batch jobs.
4) Automated rollback triggers and human-in-loop escalation at pre-defined thresholds.

Instrumentation requirements (what product/infra needs to add):
- Eval-suite automation: per-config nightly evaluations against canonical workload slices (unit tests + prompt sets + adversarial prompts). Results published to a time-series.
- Canary telemetry: per-route, per-config: success_rate, latency_p95, tokens_per_response, fallback_rate, truncated_fraction, avg_quality_score (from eval probes).
- Drift detection: rolling-window compare of quality probes vs baseline with effect-size calculation and p-values.
- Aggregated CQR metric computed per-route and exposed in Console and in the cost-model spreadsheet.

Statistical gating rules (initial proposal):
- Rapid canary auto-reject if any of:
  * latency_p95 increases > 2x AND absolute latency_p95 > 1500ms for interactive routes.
  * error_rate increase > 0.5 percentage points AND relative error increase > 2x.
  * fallback_rate increases by >= 0.3 percentage points (or relative increase > 50%) in the canary window.
  * avg_quality_score drop of >= 0.02 absolute (task-weighted quality normalized to 0..1) with p < 0.05.
- Extended silent canary to pass if:
  * avg_quality_score drop in [-0.02, 0] with p >= 0.05 AND CQR >= 15 (i.e., large cost wins for tiny quality loss).
  * OR avg_quality_score drop in [-0.01, 0] with CQR >= 8 and no customer-facing telemetry deterioration.
- Any avg_quality_score drop <= -0.03 should immediately trigger manual review and automatic rollback regardless of cost.

Why these numbers?
- We want a simple starting point that favors user experience for interactive flows while allowing higher risk for batch/low-visibility workloads. The exact thresholds will be tuned after 6–8 pilot rollouts.

Canary sample sizing guidance (simple heuristics):
- For binomial signals (fallbacks, errors), use normal approximation: to detect a change of delta p = 0.5% with 80% power at p ~1% baseline, need ~50k requests in canary window. Rapid canaries likely won't hit that, so prioritize higher-signal proxies (latency, avg_quality_score from active probes).
- For quality probes (deterministic eval prompts), run fixed N=200–1000 prompts across important slices per canary window. Use bootstrap CIs on aggregate score.

Example threshold table (text representation to be ported into spreadsheet):
- Workload: "Customer Chat (interactive)"
  * Baseline config: fp16 Llama-2-Chat-70B token-cost-per-1k = $X
  * Cheaper config candidate: q4_tuned Llama-2-Chat-70B 
  * Expected Cd: -38%
  * Eval-suite Qd observed (N=500 prompts): -0.007 (p=0.12)
  * Canary telemetry: latency_p95 +8%, fallback_rate +0.05ppt (from 0.3% to 0.35%)
  * Action: pass rapid canary, schedule 48h silent canary with CQR = 38%/0.007≈5428 -> pass policy
- Workload: "Transactional rerank (batch)"
  * Baseline: fp16 model family A
  * Candidate: smaller family B (1/3 parameters)
  * Expected Cd: -60%
  * Eval-suite Qd (N=800): -0.035 (p=0.01)
  * Action: fail auto-rollout, require human review and targeted eval to find slices driving regression; consider mid-point config (quantized plus distillation).

Spreadsheet & cost-model integration notes (how the sheets should evolve):
- Add columns per candidate config: Cd_estimate, measured_Cd (post-canary), Qd_estimate, measured_Qd, CQR, last_canary_date, canary_result (pass/fail), rollout_state.
- Add derived fields: projected_monthly_savings = measured_Cd * current_month_spend_on_route, effective_savings_after_rollbacks (apply historical rollback rate).
- Flag configs with unstable CQRs (large variance across N eval runs) as "needs more data".

Operational playbook (concise):
1) Launch rapid canary (0.5% traffic, 60m).
2) Watch automated triggers (console alert, slack #opt-rollouts).
3) If pass, promote to silent canary (5% for 48–72h) and run extended eval probes.
4) If silent canary pass, schedule staged ramp (15% -> 40% -> 100%) with monitoring at each step.
5) If a threshold trip occurs at any stage, automatic rollback to prior config and ticket created to OPT-queue.

Human-in-loop and CS signals:
- Create simple CS playbook: if a customer reports quality regression, CS should capture prompt and route to a prioritized debug queue. Cross-link to canary windows to see if their traffic overlapped.
- Provide CS with a short "explainability" card showing common failure modes for the cheaper config (e.g., hallucination increase on long instructions).

Pilot plan and metrics of success:
- Kickoff 3 pilots in next quarter: 1 high-volume interactive route, 1 async batch rerank, 1 enterprise-dedicated route with stricter SLA.
- Success criteria: 3/3 pilots use the sentry and at least 2 produce stable savings >20% with <0.015 avg_quality_score loss across 30 days.

Open questions / next steps (action items):
- [ ] Finalize the composite quality scoring function with applied-ML (weighting of prompt slices, automatic adversarial prompt generation).
- [ ] Add CQR column to the centralized cost-model spreadsheet and wire an hourly job to recalc after canaries. (Owner: Jonah)
- [ ] Implement a lightweight dashboard in Console for per-route canary metrics + an alert template (Owner: Maya).
- [ ] Run power-analysis to translate detection thresholds to minimum canary window sizes per route type (Owner: SRE).
- [ ] Socialize draft with Solutions Engineering and CS to capture customer-facing risk tolerances.

Appendix: short notes on measurement techniques
- Bootstrapping: use bootstrap confidence intervals for avg_quality_score when N < 1000, and report 90% CI on Console.
- Effect-size prioritization: prefer absolute quality delta thresholds (e.g., -0.02) rather than purely p-value driven decisions; p-values are used as supporting evidence.
- Canary probe design: include both deterministic eval prompts and randomized sampled live prompts (redacted) to catch distributional regressions.

Rough TODO timeline (3 sprints):
- Sprint 1: wire basic canary telemetry + add CQR fields in cost sheet.
- Sprint 2: implement auto-reject triggers and Console alerts; piloted with 1 route.
- Sprint 3: expand silent canary orchestration; enable staged ramps via rollout API.

Notes to reviewer:
- This is intentionally prescriptive on thresholds to get concrete experiments running; expect to iterate. Please comment with concrete objections or alternative numeric thresholds based on prior rollouts.

End of draft.
